title: Book One · Chapter 60: Two Monday Mornings
story:
Dad is ready for his first trial morning. Ronan is still putting on his shoes.

Dad carries his blue toolbox. His clean shirt is under an old work jacket. Mum gives Dad his bread packet. She asks about the card from Mr Sun.

Dad pats his pocket. “The card is here.”

Ronan follows him to the green gate. He wants Dad to have a good morning. Which words can he use? He cannot choose. He looks toward the busy road.

“Mind the cart corner,” he says.

“I will.”

Dad turns toward River Street. He has plenty of time. He walks at an easy pace. A delivery cart passes. Dad goes out of sight. Ronan goes back for his school bag.

At breakfast, Mum explains the day. Dad and Mr Sun agreed on three trial mornings. The first is today. After three mornings, Dad and Mr Sun will talk again. There may be more work. There may not be. Dad knows the pay for these three days. The work comes first. Then Dad gets the money.

“Can we be pleased now?” Ronan asks.

“Yes,” Mum says. “We can be pleased about this.”

She smiles, and he smiles back. Dad has work for today. They can be glad about that.

At school, Leo asks about the shop. “Does your dad own Mr Sun's shop now?” Ronan shakes his head and explains the counter and the trial. Leo listens. He smiles at the news of three mornings.

“My dad had a first morning at the station,” he says. “That was before I was born. He often tells us that story.”

“Does he forget the next morning?”

“He forgets his breakfast. But he remembers that first work morning.”

The boys laugh. Then Miss Wu asks them to open their books. Ronan reads the first line slowly and correctly. Dad is at work. Ronan is in class. Both have a job to do this morning.

After school, Mum takes them to Mr Qiu's stall. Mum needs to check the entrance. She is not ready to visit Mrs Gao yet. Mrs Lan is keeping the brown envelope at home. It is in her locked front-room drawer at six West Lane. Mr Han's notes are beside it.

Mr Qiu remembers another detail about East Court. The old entrance was behind the rice shop. Later, some people used a side gate. That gate was near the shop with blue bowls in its window.

“Do they still use that gate now?” Mum asks.

“I don't know. I need to check, too. I don't want to send you through a store yard.”

They look toward the corner. The blue-bowl shop is shut for its afternoon meal. A little sign gives its opening time. Mum cannot wait that long. A sewing customer is coming to her home.

They don't knock on private shutters or try the boards behind the rice shop. Mum tells the boys the next step. They need to ask at the blue-bowl shop. Which side gate can they use to reach six East Court? Then an adult must check Mrs Gao's name and door. Then an adult can bring the envelope.

Ronan writes that on the back of the map. The west route is checked. The east entrance is the one missing part. The money is still safe with Mrs Lan. They saw no theft. They will ask about the route again.

At home, Dad is washing his hands. The first morning is done. Mr Sun showed him the labels. Each job needs its owner's name first. Then Dad can begin the repair. Dad finished one small repair. Another job needs a part. That one will wait. Dad looks tired. Ronan comes in. Dad looks up and smiles.

Ronan puts the map beside him, clear of the water. Dad reads the note about the side gate.

“Do you need to ask about this gate?” he asks.

Ronan nods. The road on his map still ends before the side gate. He leaves that part blank. He needs to ask about it first.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：trial＝试工；pay＝报酬；side gate＝侧门；route＝路线。

理解问题：

1. Dad 的试工有哪些已经确定和仍未确定的部分？
2. 关于 East Court，下一步必须问清楚什么？
